difficultyRationale: Platform-estimated: EASY - one concept (the memoryless property of the exponential distribution) gives P(X > 10 | X > 5) = P(X > 5) = 0.35 by direct recall, well under 1.5 min for a prepared student.
stem: Let $X$ be an exponentially distributed random variable with mean $\lambda\,(> 0)$. If $P(X > 5) = 0.35$, then the conditional probability $P(X > 10 \mid X > 5)$ is ___________ . (Rounded off to **two** decimal places)

solution.quick: The exponential distribution is **memoryless**: $P(X > s + t \mid X > s) = P(X > t)$. With $s = t = 5$, $P(X > 10 \mid X > 5) = P(X > 5) = 0.35$. The value of $\lambda$ is never needed. Answer: **0.35**.

steps.title: Survival function of the exponential distribution
steps.body:
With mean $\lambda > 0$ (as in the question), the pdf is $f(x) = \dfrac{1}{\lambda} e^{-x/\lambda}$ for $x \ge 0$, so the survival (tail) function is

$$
P(X > x) = \int_x^{\infty} \frac{1}{\lambda} e^{-u/\lambda}\, du = e^{-x/\lambda}, \qquad x \ge 0.
$$

steps.title: Use the given information
steps.body:
$$
P(X > 5) = e^{-5/\lambda} = 0.35.
$$

(If desired, $\lambda = -5 / \ln 0.35 \approx 4.763$, but we will not need it.)

steps.title: Apply the definition of conditional probability
steps.body:
$$
P(X > 10 \mid X > 5) = \frac{P(\{X > 10\} \cap \{X > 5\})}{P(X > 5)} = \frac{P(X > 10)}{P(X > 5)},
$$

because the event $\{X > 10\}$ is contained in $\{X > 5\}$, so their intersection is just $\{X > 10\}$.

steps.title: Compute
steps.body:
$$
P(X > 10) = e^{-10/\lambda} = \left(e^{-5/\lambda}\right)^2 = 0.35^2 = 0.1225,
$$

$$
P(X > 10 \mid X > 5) = \frac{0.1225}{0.35} = 0.35.
$$

Equivalently $\dfrac{e^{-10/\lambda}}{e^{-5/\lambda}} = e^{-5/\lambda} = P(X > 5)$: this is the memoryless property. Rounded to two decimal places the answer is **0.35**, inside the official key range 0.34 to 0.36.

solution.teaching:
**The exponential distribution** models a waiting time, for example the time until a component fails or until the next customer arrives. With mean $\lambda$ its pdf is $f(x) = \frac{1}{\lambda} e^{-x/\lambda}$ for $x \ge 0$. (Many books instead write $f(x) = \lambda e^{-\lambda x}$ with $\lambda$ the *rate*, so the mean is $1/\lambda$; always check which convention a question uses. This question says the **mean** is $\lambda$.) Either way, the survival function has the form $P(X > x) = e^{-cx}$ for some constant $c > 0$.

**Memoryless property.** For any $s, t \ge 0$,

$$
P(X > s + t \mid X > s) = \frac{P(X > s + t)}{P(X > s)} = \frac{e^{-c(s+t)}}{e^{-cs}} = e^{-ct} = P(X > t).
$$

In words: if you have already waited $s$ units and nothing has happened, the chance of waiting at least $t$ **more** units is exactly the same as it was at the start. The process "does not remember" how long it has been running; a component with an exponential lifetime does not age. Among continuous distributions, the exponential is the **only** one with this property (the geometric distribution plays the same role for discrete variables).

**Why the parameter drops out.** The conditional probability depends only on the extra waiting time $t$, not on the parameter's value separately. Because $P(X > t)$ is given directly, you never need to solve for the parameter.

**Connection to this question.** Having already survived past 5, surviving past 10 needs 5 more units, so $P(X > 10 \mid X > 5) = P(X > 5) = 0.35$.
solution.shortcut: Memoryless property: $P(X > 5 + 5 \mid X > 5) = P(X > 5) = 0.35$, with no computation needed.
solution.commonTrap: Reporting the **unconditional** probability $P(X > 10) = 0.35^2 = 0.1225 \approx 0.12$ instead of dividing by $P(X > 5)$. Also avoid answering $1 - 0.35 = 0.65$, or spending time solving for $\lambda$ (and mixing up the mean and rate conventions), which is unnecessary.

answerVerification.method: Blind independent re-solve + Python check agrees with official key
answerVerification.checkCode:
import math, random
lam = -5 / math.log(0.35)                  # mean lambda from P(X>5) = exp(-5/lam) = 0.35
sf = lambda x: math.exp(-x / lam)          # survival function P(X > x)
ans = sf(10) / sf(5)                       # P(X>10 | X>5) = P(X>10)/P(X>5)
print(round(lam, 4), round(sf(10), 4), round(ans, 4))   # 4.7627 0.1225 0.35
random.seed(1); xs = [random.expovariate(1/lam) for _ in range(10**6)]
a = sum(x > 5 for x in xs); b = sum(x > 10 for x in xs)
print(round(b / a, 3))                     # Monte Carlo ~0.35
assert abs(ans - 0.35) < 1e-12 and 0.34 <= round(ans, 2) <= 0.36
answerVerification.notes: Blind re-solve (before viewing key or stored solution): by the memoryless property, P(X > 10 | X > 5) = P(X > 10)/P(X > 5) = e^{-10/λ}/e^{-5/λ} = e^{-5/λ} = P(X > 5) = 0.35; λ = -5/ln 0.35 ≈ 4.763 is not needed. Confirmed exactly and by Monte Carlo simulation in the Python check. 0.35 lies inside the official key range 0.34 to 0.36.
